questions.title: Comprehension Clause Order
questions.description: What is the correct structure of a list comprehension that also filters?
questions.Option1: [expression for variable in iterable if condition]
questions.Option2: [for variable in iterable if condition expression]
questions.Option3: [if condition for variable in iterable expression]
questions.Option4: [expression if condition for variable in iterable]

questions.title: Equivalent Loop Pairing
questions.description: Which ordinary loop produces the same list as the comprehension [x * 2 for x in nums]?
questions.Option1: result = [] then: for x in nums: result.append(x * 2)
questions.Option2: for x in nums: result = x * 2
questions.Option3: result = [] then: for x in nums: if x * 2: result.append(x)

questions.title: Comp Builds New List
questions.description: After running doubled = [x for x in nums], which statement is true?

questions.Option2: doubled is a new list; changing it never changes nums
questions.Option3: doubled is a live view that updates when nums changes
questions.Option4: doubled is an immutable tuple copy

questions.title: Set Comp Dedupe Purpose
questions.description: tags = ["sale", "flash", "sale"]. What is the most direct one-line comprehension to collect the distinct tags, and which property does that result lack?
questions.Option1: {t for t in tags}; the result is a set, so it has no defined order
questions.Option2: [t for t in tags]; it removes duplicates automatically
questions.Option3: {t: t for t in tags}; the result keeps the original tag order
questions.Option4: (t for t in tags); it materializes all unique tags at once

questions.title: If Without Else Filters
questions.description: How does [x for x in data if x > 0] differ from [x if x > 0 else 0 for x in data]?
questions.Option1: The first keeps only the positive values; the second keeps every element, replacing negatives with 0
questions.Option3: The first replaces negatives with 0; the second drops them

questions.title: Transpose Comp Output
questions.description: What does this snippet print?

print([[row[j] for row in m] for j in range(3)])

questions.title: Stacked Ifs Comp Output
questions.description: A comprehension can carry several if clauses in a row. What does this snippet print?
questions.codesnippet: print([x for x in range(20) if x % 2 == 0 if x % 3 == 0])

questions.title: Exhausted Generator Sum
questions.description: What does this snippet print? (A generator expression can be consumed only once.)
questions.codesnippet:
g = (x for x in range(3))
print(sum(g) + sum(g))
